narrative: OMX30 opens to a synchronized global rally: Europe and Asia both bid, NASDAQ up 1.30%, Nikkei surging 2.08%. The index sits 9.7% above its 200-day MA in a confirmed bull market, with MACD above signal and ADX at 69.9 signaling strong directional conviction. However, RSI at 84.86 and Stochastic K/D both >83 represent extreme overbought conditions — textbook mean-reversion setup. Commodities are mixed-to-positive (gold +1.75%, copper +1.00% for mining plays; oil flat), and falling yields (US 10Y -0.21%) reduce refinancing and DCF drag. The main headwind is SEK strength (USD/SEK -0.32%), which pressures large exporters. We expect a small positive open (+0.4% to +0.6%), but watch for profit-taking given technical extremes.
morningBrief: OMX30 set for a modest gap-up open around +0.5% as global momentum flows in: DAX, NASDAQ, and Nikkei all strong overnight. The index is within 0.4% of its 52-week high (3185), trading 9.7% above the 200-MA, but RSI 84.86 and Stochastic K/D >83 are screaming overbought — expect pullback attempts toward 3123 (yesterday's close) or 3100 support if early rally falters. Key watch: ADX 69.9 remains extremely strong, so bears need a break below the 50-MA (≈3150) to challenge the bull. Sector calls: Boliden a clear long (gold +1.75%, copper +1.00%); Industrials + Volvo/Atlas benefit from commodity stability but face SEK headwind (USD/SEK -0.32%); Banks neutral (yields down slightly); Tech cautious into such elevated technicals. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET — if softer than expected, expect vol spike. Tight stops above 3185; target any dip toward 3115–3125 for intraday longs.
